title: Maps canvas composition
question: The world is Living Grammar. Lock the composition for maps.spellkave.com: map as canvas, grant-gated layers, no Play mosaic.

options.label: Picker first
options.thesis: The map stays quiet until you pick a place; the picker card is the whole chrome.
options.viewport: Full-bleed map. A loom-card at the lower third names the picked place, my seat, and floor. Grant-gated layer chips sit under that card. Observer inspect opens from one gold commit on the card. Seat seal top-right.
options.risk: A player who only wants to pan the world is forced through a picker before layers feel present.

raised.raise: Floor rides the picker as a depth readout, not a separate widget.
One gold commit on the picker opens inspect; nothing else on the card is an action.

options.label: Forecast strip
options.thesis: The map is the world; a thin edge strip is the only layer UI, like Windy’s What.
materials: bottom timeline when radar is on
options.viewport: Full-bleed map. Left strip lists only grant-allowed layers; occupancy on for observers, radar off. Floor is the strip’s level control. Click a place or pin to open a right drawer. Radar, if turned on, takes a bottom timeline. Seat seal top-right.
options.risk: Closest to the confirmed brief, so it can feel like we skipped choosing.

options.label: Concentric watch
options.thesis: Your seat is the center; each grant is a ring you can light: place, occupancy, radar.
options.viewport: Full-bleed map centered on my seat. Inner ring is place and seat. Observer outer ring is occupancy pins. Radar is a time ring, off at first paint. Selecting a pin isolates it and dims the rest into an inspect drawer. Seat seal top-right.
options.risk: Rings fight the cartography; a world without a seat has no center.
